name: Michigan
metaDescription: Check Michigan hunting dates for 2026–27, including deer, elk, bear, turkey and waterfowl, with DNR license fees, education and draw information.

intro: Michigan publishes a statewide calendar, but many opportunities still depend on deer management units, elk management units, bear management units, turkey management units or waterfowl zones. Use the calendar for the broad date, then open the species digest to confirm your unit and tag.
zoneNote: Deer tags and antler restrictions differ by DMU/county and Upper versus Lower Peninsula; elk and bear are limited to selected management units and drawn licenses; fall turkey is limited to TMUs I and M; waterfowl dates vary by zone and special goose units.

licenseAndEducation.fact: Annual base hunting license is required unless an exception applies; it allows small-game hunting and purchase of additional licenses. Official fees: junior $6, resident $11, nonresident $151, resident senior $5. Buy via the DNR Hunt Fish app, eLicense or a license agent. Tags bought online may take 10–15 business days; store tags are immediately usable.

First-time hunters born on or after Jan. 1, 1960 must pass hunter safety before buying a base license, except for the apprentice-license pathway. DNR lists classroom/field-day and online/home-study options.

Michigan has apprentice and mentored youth opportunities with age, mentor proximity, equipment and species-specific rules. The DNR fee page lists the mentored youth hunting license at $7.50; review the species digest before relying on an exception.

Official fee page lists deer $20; deer combo $40 resident/$190 nonresident/$28 senior; antlerless deer $20; fall/spring turkey $15 or $6 senior; waterfowl $12; federal duck stamp $28; fur harvester $15 or $6 senior; nonresident small-game 3-day $50/7-day $80; bear application $5/license $25; elk application $5/license $100.
DNR offers digital eHarvest tags through the Hunt Fish app. Paper tags bought online are mailed; tags printed by license agents can be used immediately.
Hunters age 16+ need a Michigan waterfowl license and federal duck stamp; HIP/migratory-bird registration is free and required. The 2026 electronic federal stamp is valid July 1, 2026–June 30, 2027.
